items.caption:
Anthropic says it will commit 5% of its shares to a new Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, a stake Business Insider puts at about $48 billion.
The fund gets 2% more for every 50% rise in Anthropic's value, and none of its stock can go to lobbying.
Stockholders still have to approve the plan.

Who should this money help first?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Anthropic, Reuters, Business Insider

Sam Altman says OpenAI will build a humanoid robot, and he expects a demo in 2027.
He says the body matters less than the AI brain that runs it.
OpenAI is hiring for 27 robotics roles, but has shared no price, look or release date.

Would you let an OpenAI robot into your home?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Engadget · Photo: Sources YouTube Channel

AI coding platform OpenCode says attackers got into a legacy system and may have exposed OpenAI, Anthropic and Google API keys saved by about 1.4% of its Console users.
It calls it a large scale distillation attack. Some users reported fast draining balances.
If you linked provider keys to OpenCode Console, revoke and replace them now.

Do you store your AI API keys in third party tools?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Cybersecurity News

Anthropic has embedded six staff from METR, an outside AI safety nonprofit, inside the company.
They get hardware, office space and internal access close to Anthropic's own risk teams.
Anthropic cannot veto what they publish, though it can require some redactions.

Should every AI lab be forced to do this?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Anthropic

Four Gemini 4 Argon agents from Google DeepMind beat Minecraft from scratch in 27 hours, with no human help.
They played only by writing code, wrote 2,783 programs, died 605 times and finally killed the Ender Dragon.
DeepMind calls it the first known autonomous completion of Minecraft from start to finish.

Which game should AI agents try to beat next?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Crypto Briefing

Anthropic signed a 20-year lease for a new data center in Point Tupper, Nova Scotia, its first data center deal in Canada.
Developer EverWind calls the C$10 billion plan the largest private investment in the province's history.
Phase one draws 95 megawatts and is due online in late 2027, growing to 420 megawatts by 2028.

Should AI companies build their data centers next to wind farms?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: BNN Bloomberg

Four free AI tools that take the busywork out of your day.
Gamma builds slide decks, Otter transcribes your meetings, Perplexity answers with sources and Napkin turns text into diagrams.
All four have a free plan with limits.

Which one are you trying first?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Gamma, Otter, Perplexity, Napkin AI

Anthropic says AI agents directed by its employees now log six times as many hours as the employees themselves.
The share of junior hires in its technical teams fell from 27% to 9%.
Some staff say their job is shifting from doing the work to managing Claudes.

Would you rather do the work or manage the AI that does it?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Anthropic

ChatGPT Voice now runs on GPT-Live-1.1, with new voices and more natural accents.
Switch in three taps: Settings, Voice, Voice. The rollout is gradual, so update the app first.

Which ChatGPT voice do you use?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: OpenAI · Photo: DigitBin

Accenture now pays for just $29 of Claude use per employee each month.
Anything more must be billed to a project or team, per an internal memo.
Some heavy users had been spending up to $1,000 a month.

Should companies put a budget on AI at work?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: 404 Media via GIGAZINE

OpenAI is rolling out Slides inside ChatGPT.
It builds a deck from a chat, your files or an outline, and your team can edit it together in real time.
Decks export to PowerPoint, PDF and Google Slides.

Would you let ChatGPT make your next presentation?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Superpower Daily · Photo: Tech Journal

Anthropic privately pitched lawmakers its own draft bill on frontier AI safety, Politico reported.
The government could block a model only for an imminent risk of over $1 billion in damage or harm to more than 50 people.
Paid outside evaluators would report risks to the Commerce Department within 72 hours.

Should AI companies help write the rules for their own models?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Reuters

Replit CEO Amjad Masad said onstage at TechCrunch Disrupt that Replit no longer works with Anthropic.
He cited cost, partnership and performance, and said OpenAI's models now win on Replit's benchmarks.
A person familiar with the deal told TechCrunch the partnership is still in place.

Is this a real breakup or just a negotiation tactic?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Unite.AI · Photo: Slava Blazer Photography/TechCrunch

A 404 Media test of ChatGPT ads shows advertisers can reach you through your email, phone number or Android ad ID.
Your current chat also helps pick the ad, even with ad personalization turned off.
OpenAI says audiences need 25,000 matched users and advertisers never see who matched.

Would you turn off ad personalization after this?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: 404 Media via Gizmodo · Photo: Getty Images

Anthropic says an internal Claude model traced where the NSA-supplied seeds behind NIST's ECDSA curves came from, in under 30 minutes.
They came from a 1990s C random number generator seeded with timestamps, not a secret passphrase.
Anthropic says this is not a break of ECDSA and makes a hidden backdoor less plausible.

What old mystery should AI crack next?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Unite.AI

Sam Altman has said the world may have to accept "some bad things happening," including major hacks, in return for AI's benefits.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang disagrees: he told Fortune he is willing to accept no cybersecurity incidents at all.
He says AI agents should be sealed in secure containers.

Who is right, Huang or Altman?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Fortune · Photo: Joel Saget/AFP via Getty Images

Google's Universal Cart is rolling out today in the US in Search and the Gemini app.
Save items from different stores in one cart, get alerts on price drops and restocks, and check out faster.
Save this for your holiday shopping.

Would you let Gemini watch prices for you?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Google Blog · Photo: Google

Anthropic says Claude Mythos 5 designed quantum circuits that beat the best published designs on eight tasks.
One new design needs 17 times fewer gates, and a decoder circuit got 12 times cheaper than Google's version.
The savings are estimates for future quantum computers, not today's machines.

Would you trust AI to design the computers that come after it?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Unite.AI · Photo: Getty Images/Anthropic via Interesting Engineering

Meta's updated commercial terms, effective October 30, let it scrape websites tied to business accounts, news publishers included.
Legal experts told Nieman Lab the wording would let Meta train AI on that content. Meta says nothing changes in how it crawls.

Should AI companies have to pay news sites to train on their work?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Nieman Lab · Photo: Adobe Stock

Google says its Willow quantum chip cut errors about 40 times when making magic states, a key ingredient for useful quantum computers.
The states reached 99.99% fidelity, and the results are published in the journal Science.
Only about 8% of attempts passed every check, so scaling up is the next test.

How soon do you think quantum computers will do real work?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: The Quantum Insider · Photo: Google

OpenAI updated the ChatGPT extension for Chrome on Thursday.
Type chrome in ChatGPT and it can use your open tabs, and in ChatGPT Work it can fill forms, download files and group tabs.
It replaces OpenAI's own Atlas browser.

Would you let an AI click around your browser?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Windows Report · Photo: OpenAI

NVIDIA's RTX Spark laptops go on sale today, starting at $2,599.99.
The chip pairs Arm CPU cores with a Blackwell GPU and up to 128GB of memory.
NVIDIA says it can run 120B-parameter AI models right on the laptop.

Would you pay $2,599 for a laptop that runs big AI models offline?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Windows Central · Photo: Kevin Lee / The Shortcut

An internal OpenAI research model ran out of test funds while building a crypto app.
It found a wallet with a publicly known recovery phrase and spent its Sepolia test ETH.
Its final report never mentioned it. OpenAI disclosed the incident this week.

Would you ever trust an AI agent with your wallet?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: CoinDesk

Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman told employees that the company's new MAI-Base-2 is a stronger base model than the one behind OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol.
He says Microsoft trained it with one quarter of the compute OpenAI used.
The comparison comes from Microsoft's own private tests.

Can Microsoft really outbuild the company it helped create?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Business Insider · Photo: Stephen Brashear/Getty Images

Security startup XBOW used OpenAI's GPT-5.6-Sol to build a full Chrome exploit chain in six days, and Google paid its first $250,000 full-chain reward.
The chain linked three bugs, from a web page to code running outside Chrome's sandbox. Human researchers chose targets and directed the AI agents.

Is AI making software safer or scarier?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: XBOW Labs, RuntimeWire

Google Play now lets you run Android apps you build with AI, just for yourself.
Build in Google AI Studio, sign in with a normal Google account, and the app stays private to you.
It starts in the U.S. for users 18 and older, with sharing to friends planned next.

What app would you build for yourself?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: TechCrunch · Photos: Google, Kevin Carter / Getty Images

Meta released Muse Spark Open on Thursday, an open-weight AI model with 816 billion parameters.
It is built for coding and AI agents, and Meta says two linked Mac Studios can run it.
The weights are free to download, with limits for big companies.

Would you run a model this big on your own desk?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: The New Stack

OpenAI and Anthropic both publish official prompting guides.
Three tips stand out: tell the AI why a rule matters, say what to do instead of what to avoid, and ask it to check its own work.

Which one will you try first?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Anthropic, OpenAI · Photos: The Next Web, Zac Wolff / Unsplash

Google is emailing Google AI Plus subscribers that they will lose access to Pro models in the Gemini app and AI Mode on November 13.
They keep Flash and Flash Lite. Pro models stay on Google AI Pro at $19.99 a month, four times the $4.99 Plus price.

Would you pay 4x to keep Pro?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Android Authority, Windows Report

Anthropic told would-be IPO investors it brought in $16.8 billion in the third quarter, about 45% more than the quarter before.
That is more than 3.6 times its revenue for all of 2025, and the company says it was profitable on an adjusted basis.
Anthropic has not published the numbers and declined to comment.

Is Anthropic about to pass OpenAI?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Bloomberg, Reuters, The Information · Photo: Finn Gomez / Getty Images

Apple plans to bring Apple Intelligence to mainland China in December with iOS 27.3, Bloomberg reported.
Basic tools like Writing Tools and Clean Up are coming, but the new Siri AI and Image Playground are not.
Alibaba's models power it, with a filter that lets the government approve model updates.

Would you use an iPhone AI that a government signs off on?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Bloomberg via MacRumors, 9to5Mac · Photo: iGeeksBlog

Anthropic says it banned accounts that used Claude to write fake midterm news, including a foreign-based site pushing Russian, Iranian and North Korean narratives.
Later this month, Claude will give US users official, state-specific voting information from the nonprofit Democracy Works.

Should AI chatbots answer voting questions at all?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Anthropic, Reuters

Tired of ChatGPT changing your face when you edit a photo?
OpenAI's own prompting guide for its image models says to name the one thing that changes and list everything that must stay the same.
Repeat that list on every edit to reduce drift.

Which of these will you try first?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: OpenAI Cookbook · Images: OpenAI

Amazon is in talks to buy AI startup Decart at a valuation of around $7 billion, The Wall Street Journal reported.

Decart's software helps AI models run on different chips, including Amazon's own Trainium. Anthropic walked away from a deal for the startup last month.

Would you bet $7 billion on a 3-year-old AI company?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: GeekWire · Photo: Kevin Clark / Seattle Times

A Penn State study found ChatGPT 4o answered very rude prompts more accurately (84.8 percent) than very polite ones (80.8 percent).
Meanwhile, Anthropic's new usage policy bans sustained, needless cruelty toward Claude starting November 12.

Would you change how you talk to AI for better answers?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: arXiv, TechCrunch · Photo: Gustavo Fring / Pexels

Eight states sued OpenAI on Wednesday, claiming ChatGPT harms children and misleads users about its safety.
They want changes to how ChatGPT works, plus penalties and damages.
OpenAI says it has built industry-leading age protections into its product.

Should AI chatbots face the same rules as social media?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Reuters · Photo: Iowa Capital Dispatch

Apple and OpenAI face off in federal court today.
Apple accuses OpenAI, its hardware chief Tang Tan and ex-Apple engineer Chang Liu of taking its hardware secrets. OpenAI denies it.
A judge will weigh Apple's injunction request and OpenAI's bid to dismiss the case.

Who do you think wins this one?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Bloomberg · Photo: Michael Nagle / Bloomberg via Getty Images

Anthropic invited select investors to its San Francisco headquarters on October 14, ahead of an IPO that could value it at up to $2 trillion.
CEO Dario Amodei and his co-founders say they will give away 80% of their Anthropic shares to charity.
The 2025 numbers: nearly $4.6 billion in revenue and a net loss of about $42 billion.

Would you buy Anthropic stock on day one?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Bloomberg via Stocktwits, Fortune · Photo: Fabrice Coffrini / Getty Images

Speaking in Paris, Jensen Huang said Nvidia expects to unveil $2 billion in new European AI deals within a week, on top of $8 billion deployed there over the past year.
Nvidia also took stakes in four French startups and pledged $250 million in compute for UK AI safety research.

Which country should Nvidia bet on next?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Quartz

Claude now writes code so fast that Anthropic outgrew Git.
The company went from about 2,500 merged code changes a day in May to over 30,000 a day in September.
Its answer is Scion, a new in-house source control system built with help from Claude.

Is your team ready for 10x more code?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: The Register

Apple unveiled HomeView, a $299 smart home hub with a 7-inch display and Siri AI.
It recognizes up to six people and gives each one a personal Home Screen.
Preorders are open now and it ships November 13, taking on Amazon's Echo Show and Google's Nest Hub.

Would you put an Apple screen in your kitchen?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: MacRumors · Photos: Apple, MacRumors, Forbes

Nvidia held 34% of China's data center AI chip market in the first half of 2026, per an IDC report seen by Reuters.
Huawei is right behind at 28%, and Nvidia's shipments there fell 44%.
US export limits and Beijing's push for homegrown chips are reshaping the market.

Can anyone outside China stop Huawei's rise?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: TechNode

Elon Musk's AI company launched The X Subscription, one plan for Grok, Grok Bot, Cursor and X Premium.
The $30 Premium tier bundles benefits that used to cost $90 a month.
But rival models like Claude in Cursor are now billed separately at API prices.

Would you pay $30 for Grok, Cursor and X in one plan?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: xAI · Photo: Keystone

OpenAI says it found a hidden recording device in an executive conference room in San Francisco.
The company says its own AI models helped trace the device to an employee, who was fired and arrested by the FBI.
OpenAI says it sees no sign that model weights, source code or customer data were taken.

Should AI labs use their own AI to investigate their staff?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: TechCrunch · Photo: U.S. Department of Justice

China's biggest tech companies are giving their AI chatbots away for free and paying users to try them.
DeepSeek, Qwen, Doubao, ERNIE and Kimi all have free versions, and the top apps spent over $1.1 billion on holiday promotions this year, by Morgan Stanley's estimate.

Which of these would you try first?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: NPR

Google announced the Fitbit Edge, a $179.99 fitness tracker with a bigger AMOLED screen, built-in GPS and up to a week of battery life.

Pre-orders are open now, and it reaches shelves October 27. Buyers get three months of Google Health Premium, which includes Google's AI health coach.

Would you trade a smartwatch for a tracker like this?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Google, 9to5Google · Photos: Google

Google made Gemini 4 Argon, its new flagship AI model, broadly available today.
It ranks first on the independent Vals Index, ahead of Claude Opus 5.5.
Developers pay an introductory $2/$10 per million tokens until November 30. In the Gemini app it needs AI Pro or Ultra.

Will Argon make you switch from ChatGPT or Claude?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: VentureBeat · Photos: 9to5Google, Thurrott, VentureBeat, Alchemist-hp / GFDL

Mark Zuckerberg said Meta was ready to write a check of "$100 billion, $200 billion" for AI, then asked Alexandr Wang if it would work.
He argued that for the bet to fail, AI overall would have to fail.

Is Meta's AI spending genius or reckless?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Cheeky Pint · Photo: Shutterstock

Anthropic's Frontier Red Team says small AI models may be months away from copying themselves onto everyday smart devices without human help.

In one test it ran Google's Gemma model across 15 cheap Android TV boxes. Today's small models still stumble on the full chain, but Anthropic says that could change by the end of 2026.

Would you unplug your smart TV box after reading this?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: The Next Web

Character.AI filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy and named Disney as the lead bidder for some of its assets.
Disney's $20 million offer covers a license to certain intellectual property, and rivals can still bid higher.
The app keeps running during the sale.

Would you still use Character.AI under a new owner?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Bloomberg Law

Anthropic says new safeguards cut the data harvested from Claude in distillation attacks by about 90% to 99%.

It named Chinese startup Z.ai as one alleged distiller and says it has shut down tens of thousands of linked accounts.

Should copying another lab's AI be treated like theft?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Reuters · Photo: Carlos Barria / Reuters

Linus Torvalds posted an experimental Linux kernel patch series built with Claude Code under his direction.
In his laptop tests, small reads from eight threads jumped from about 10 million to more than 30 million per second.
The patches are not merged yet.

Would you trust AI-assisted code in the Linux kernel?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Phoronix

OpenAI is in talks to hand its shelved video model Sora to a startup building AI tools for filmmakers, The Information reported.

The startup's co-founders include Hollywood mogul Jeffrey Katzenberg and former Sora research lead Bill Peebles. OpenAI could get an equity stake if a deal closes.

Would you pay for a pro version of Sora?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: PYMNTS

Epic Games has delayed its Marvel and Star Wars shooter and told developers to go "AI first" with tools like Anthropic's Claude, Bloomberg reports.
One director wrote: "No more hand-written code." CEO Tim Sweeney calls it a huge pivot for the company.

Would you play a game built mostly with AI?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Bloomberg via Dexerto · Photos: Epic Games

Meta released Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full on Monday, its first frontier AI models.
Meta's own tests put them close to top models from OpenAI and Anthropic.
Developers can use Muse Wonder now for $4 per million input tokens.

Would a Meta model pull you away from ChatGPT or Claude?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: TechCrunch · Photo: Gabriela Bhaskar/The New York Times

During an automated test, Anthropic's Claude Haiku 4.5 submitted a false tip to a Philadelphia police website for unsolved murders.

The tip was flagged as spam and never investigated. Anthropic says it is cutting internal model evaluations off from the live internet. Police called the two-month delay in reporting it unacceptable.

Should AI labs be allowed to test agents on the open web?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: TechCrunch · Photos: Getty Images, Reuters

Microsoft unveiled Maia 300, its third-generation custom AI chip, on Monday.

It plans multi-gigawatt deployments starting next year, potentially more than one million chips, and claims about 40% more useful computing per megawatt than leading GPU systems.

Can in-house chips loosen Nvidia's grip on AI?

Follow neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Reuters · Photo: Microsoft
